clue.text: Taking first step, carrying a copper vessel

indicators.note: taking away the first means the opening letter of the following word is removed
something carrying a load holds it inside, so the shortened word wraps round what follows

blocks.note: taken as written, before losing its first letter
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A cautious first step, carefully carrying a copper pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking first' looks like part of the surface's first step, but it tells you to drop the opening letter of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup for drinking tea is a small container, which a vessel broadly is.

clue.text: Bailiwick that includes bridge

blocks.note: first meaning: one's area of expertise or special interest
second meaning: the enclosed steering cabin on a ship's bridge

explanation.walkthrough: The same word is idiomatic for a field of competence ('right in my ...') and literal for a ship's steering cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiwick is a person's own domain, the idiomatic sense; on a ship the steering cabin forms the bridge itself.

clue.text: Clogs loused-up, quantity of engine suppressed

indicators.note: something messed up is thrown into disorder, so the preceding word is rearranged
something suppressed is held down within, so the engine quantity sits inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
cc, cubic capacity, measures an engine's size

explanation.surface: A wrecked engine whose clogged parts have choked its power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loused-up' reads as one slang adjective but splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To occlude is to block or obstruct a passage, the same as clogging it.

clue.text: Arch conservative woman

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
Amber is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A sly, knowing woman of conservative views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' poses as an adjective meaning sly, but it is the noun for a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is a slight convex curve, as across a road surface, so it forms a gentle arch.

clue.text: Part of engine hits back, thousands missing, hot on tail

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from right to left
with something missing, those letters are left out of the word

blocks.note: to smack is to hit
K is a thousand, so thousands are Ks; these letters are removed
H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps
aft is the rear or tail of a ship

explanation.surface: A racing car's engine part fails: it strikes back, loses thousands, and the heat sits at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'thousands' removes two letters, both K and the S that makes it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A camshaft is the rotating rod carrying cams that opens and closes valves inside a motor.

clue.text: Mother fusses around Schumacher’s final two controllers

indicators.note: the final two means only the last pair of letters of the name is kept
going around something means enclosing it within

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
to nag is to fuss at someone persistently
the last two letters of the racing driver's surname

explanation.surface: A racing driver's mother frets over Michael Schumacher's last couple of team bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Schumacher is the seven-times Formula One champion; only the tail of his name is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Managers are people who run and direct a business or team, so they are its controllers.

clue.text: Turns of speech I can eschew

indicators.note: 'of' here means consisting of part of the words that follow, so the answer is found inside them

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word, the next two whole words and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone vows to avoid certain figures of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns of speech' looks like a set phrase, but 'Turns' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanes are tight sequences of bends on a racing circuit, deliberately added to slow cars.

clue.text: Nabs points on way back

indicators.note: going back means the combined letters are read from the end

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
E and N are compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Someone picks up points on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the points after the way: STEN, which read backwards gives NETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To net someone is to catch them as if in a net, which is to nab or capture.

clue.text: Lando finally attached to significant other, taking husband somewhere in the West End

indicators.note: finally means just the last letter of the name is used
taking something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: SO is the common abbreviation for significant other, a partner
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
the last letter of Lando Norris's first name

explanation.surface: The F1 driver Lando Norris and his partner, husband in tow, head out to central London.
explanation.walkthrough: SO and O join, with H slipped between them. The West End is London's theatre and entertainment district.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of central London lying within the area known for theatres, restaurants and nightlife.

clue.text: Doctor is able to retire and love country

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the word goes in the backward direction

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
can means is able to
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A doctor who can finally retire and enjoy a country he loves.
explanation.walkthrough: Monaco suits the Formula One theme: its Grand Prix runs through the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaco is a tiny sovereign principality on the Riviera, so it is a nation-state in its own right.

clue.text: Reconnect the power of French grip

blocks.note: de is French for of
to clutch is to grip

explanation.surface: Someone restores the power behind a firm French handshake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' could be a link word, but it belongs with 'French'.
explanation.definitionFit: To declutch is to release and then re-engage a vehicle's clutch, cutting and restoring drive from engine to wheels.

clue.text: Firstly, Hamilton is going home having proposed with shrill voice

indicators.note: firstly means only the opening letters of the next few words are used

blocks.note: the initials of these four words
to pitch an idea is to propose it

explanation.surface: Lewis Hamilton heads home after popping the question, squealing with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having proposed' suggests marriage but means put forward an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-pitched sound is one at the top of the audible range, describing a thin shrill tone.

clue.text: Rear illuminations sicken novice wearing hosiery

indicators.note: something wearing clothes is inside them, so these letters go within the garment word

blocks.note: to ail is to be or make unwell
L for learner, as on L-plates
tights are a form of hosiery

explanation.surface: Seeing a learner in tights makes you queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novice' as L comes from the L-plates British learner drivers must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Tail lights are the red lamps at the back of a vehicle, lighting it up from behind.

clue.text: Privileged pet name taken by our little Edward

blocks.note: hon, short for honey, is a term of endearment
taken as written
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A family's little boy Edward has a sweet nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' suggests an animal's name but here means an endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: To be honoured to do something is to feel privileged, granted a special favour or distinction.

clue.text: One who backtracks about a poet?

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a verser is one who writes verse

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a poet is a person who goes back on his word.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the rare word for a versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes into reverse moves or turns backwards, retracing their path or retreating from a position.

clue.text: Make cockup, assuming miles to reach Italy

indicators.note: one word assuming another takes it on and wraps around it

blocks.note: far, as in miles away
to err is to make a mistake, a cockup
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Someone blunders while driving the long miles to Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' poses as a verb but is the noun for a car brand. A cockup is a British slang word for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrari is an Italian brand of car, and a make is a manufacturer's brand of vehicle.

clue.text: Powers with electric current replaced by dirty air from European country

indicators.note: something dirty is disordered or messed up, so the letters are rearranged
replaced by means one letter is swapped out for others

blocks.note: Austin Powers is the spoof spy of the film series
I is the symbol for electric current
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Electrical power lines whose current is swapped for polluted air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powers' reads as electrical energy but is the surname of the comic film spy. AUSTIN's I gives way to RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Austrian is the adjective for something belonging to or coming out of Austria, a nation in central Europe.

clue.text: Inclination to be ahead, converting pole after pole

indicators.note: converting something changes its form, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: up means ahead, as in one up
S is the south pole
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver eager to lead turns pole position after pole position into wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole after pole' evokes qualifying in pole position; the first pole is S, the second is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An upslope is a rising gradient, and an inclination can mean a slope or incline.

clue.text: Track resolvent liquid after Spanish approval

indicators.note: liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so these letters can be poured into a new order

blocks.note: sí is Spanish for yes
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemist adds a dissolving liquid once the Spanish say yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolvent liquid' reads as a chemical solvent, but 'liquid' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverstone is the motor-racing circuit in Northamptonshire that hosts the British Grand Prix.

clue.text: Barmaid endlessly showing up with nothing on

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its last letter
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: only the second half of this word, maid, is wordplay: a lass is a girl or maid
O is zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barmaid turns up for work wearing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barmaid' must be split: 'Bar' is the definition and 'maid' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a public bar, especially the plusher lounge room of a pub.

clue.text: Initially, braking and traction system is not all there

indicators.note: initially means only the first letters of the following words are used

blocks.note: the initials of these four words

explanation.surface: A car's braking and traction control is only partly working.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is informal for crazy or eccentric, and not all there is an idiom for mentally unsound.

clue.text: Senna’s first to discredit the lead

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the name is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of Ayrton Senna's surname
to tar someone is to smear their reputation

explanation.surface: Ayrton Senna was first to undermine the race leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lead' suggests the front of a race, but it is the principal performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a film or play is its principal performer, the person playing the leading role.

clue.text: Best friend’s fractured large toe

indicators.note: something fractured is broken apart, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A close friend has broken their big toe.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego can mean an intimate and trusted companion, a second self, besides a person's other persona.

clue.text: Distresses using some radial arm saws

indicators.note: some means just a portion of the following words is used

blocks.note: running from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: Powerful workshop saws are upsetting to operate.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to frighten or worry them, causing distress.

clue.text: Removing protective gear, see Verstappen’s dubious lackeys

indicators.note: removing means taking those letters out of the name that follows
something dubious is unreliable or suspect, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: PPE is personal protective equipment
the driver's surname with its possessive S

explanation.surface: Max Verstappen strips off his racing gear in front of his questionable entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: VERSTAPPENS without P, P and E leaves VERSTANS to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackeys are servile attendants or footmen, people employed to wait on others.

clue.text: Viennese driver’s spoken with more colour

indicators.note: spoken means the name is said out loud and heard as another word

blocks.note: Niki Lauda was the Austrian racing champion born in Vienna

explanation.surface: An Austrian racing driver speaks more vividly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the surname and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud can describe garish, vivid clothing, so louder means showier and more brightly coloured.
